---
# Title, subtitle and author are written on the cover page in the document
# body (see "COVER PAGE" below), so they are not set here; a YAML title would
# add an extra title block above the cover.
# Report: Fishing in the English Channel and southern North Sea
output:
  word_document:
    reference_docx: "../report_template.dotx"
    toc: false        # TOC field is inserted after the version history instead
---


```{r setup, include=FALSE}

# ---- Check that the Word template exists ------------------------------------
# Must match reference_docx in the YAML header.
template_rel <- "../report_template.dotx"

# Pandoc resolves the path relative to the Rmd file, so check it from there.
# When chunks are run interactively, current_input() is NULL; fall back to
# the working directory.
rmd_dir <- if (!is.null(knitr::current_input(dir = TRUE))) {
  dirname(knitr::current_input(dir = TRUE))
} else {
  getwd()
}
template_path <- normalizePath(file.path(rmd_dir, template_rel), mustWork = FALSE)

if (!file.exists(template_path)) {
  stop("Word template not found: ", template_path,
       "\nCheck reference_docx in the YAML header, or copy the template to that location.",
       call. = FALSE)
}

# ---- Check that the output .docx can be overwritten -------------------------
# Pandoc fails at the very end of the knit if the previous output is still
# open in Word (Windows locks open files). Check this up front instead.
rmd_input <- knitr::current_input(dir = TRUE)

if (!is.null(rmd_input)) {                     # only when knitting, not interactively
  out_docx <- file.path(rmd_dir,
                        sub("\\.[Rr]md$", ".docx", basename(rmd_input)))

  if (file.exists(out_docx)) {
    writable <- tryCatch({
      con <- file(out_docx, open = "ab")       # open for appending: writes nothing,
      close(con)                               # but fails if the file is locked
      TRUE
    }, error = function(e) FALSE, warning = function(w) FALSE)

    if (!writable) {
      stop("Output file is locked (probably open in Word): ", out_docx,
           "\nClose the document in Word and knit again.",
           call. = FALSE)
    }
  }
}

load_object <- function(filepath, object_name = NULL) {
  local({
    e <- new.env()
    load(filepath, envir = e)
    if (is.null(object_name)) {
      objects <- ls(e)
      if (length(objects) == 1) {
        e[[objects]]
      } else {
        stop("File contains ", length(objects), " objects (",
             paste(objects, collapse=", "),
             "). Please specify object_name.")
      }
    } else {
      e[[object_name]]
    }
  })
}

# msg() — like message() but flushes immediately to the RStudio console.
# Useful when running chunks interactively: without flush.console(), messages
# from inside long-running blocks are buffered and only appear after the block
# completes, making it look like nothing is happening.
msg <- function(...) {
  message(...)
  flush.console()
}

apply_flag_other <- function(df, flag_col = "vessel_flag",
                              days_col = "fishing_days") {
  df %>%
    group_by(across(all_of(flag_col))) %>%
    mutate(total_flag_days = sum(.data[[days_col]])) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    mutate(
      total_days = sum(.data[[days_col]]),
      flag_pct   = total_flag_days / total_days * 100,
      across(all_of(flag_col),
             ~ if_else(flag_pct < threshold_pct, "Other", .x))
    )
}

map_gear_aer <- function(x) {
  dplyr::recode(str_to_upper(str_trim(x)),
    DTS = "Bottom trawl/seine", TBB = "Beam trawl",
    PEL = "Midwater trawl",     DFN = "Gillnet",
    HOK = "Handline/rod",       FPO = "Pot/trap",
    DRB = "Dredge",             PS  = "Purse seine",
    LL  = "Longline",
    .default = "Other/mixed"
  )
}

# UK length groups -> AER vessel length classes (lower bound of each group)
map_length_uk <- function(x) {
  lb <- suppressWarnings(readr::parse_number(x))   # "Unknown" -> NA
  dplyr::case_when(
    lb <  10 ~ "VL0010",
    lb <  12 ~ "VL1012",
    lb <  18 ~ "VL1218",
    lb <  24 ~ "VL1824",
    lb <  40 ~ "VL2440",
    lb >= 40 ~ "VL40XX",
    TRUE     ~ NA_character_
  )
}

# UK gear categories -> AER gear categories (as returned by map_gear_aer)
map_gear_uk <- function(x) {
  lookup <- c(
    "Beam trawl"           = "Beam trawl",
    "Demersal trawls"      = "Bottom trawl/seine",
    "Demersal seine"       = "Bottom trawl/seine",
    "Dredge"               = "Dredge",
    "Drift and fixed nets" = "Gillnet",
    "Handlines"            = "Handline/rod",
    "Longlines"            = "Handline/rod",
    "Pots and traps"       = "Pot/trap",
    "Pelagic seine"        = "Purse seine",
    "Pelagic trawls"       = "Other/mixed",
    "Other mobile gears"   = "Other/mixed",
    "Other passive gears"  = "Other/mixed",
    "Unknown"              = "Other/mixed"
  )
  dplyr::recode(str_trim(x), !!!lookup, .default = "Other/mixed")
}

# Harmonise species codes that differ between AER and UK for the same species
harmonise_species <- function(code) {
  dplyr::case_when(
    code %in% c("HOM", "JAX")                           ~ "JAX",
    code %in% c("CTC", "CTL")                           ~ "CTL",
    code %in% c("MON", "ANF", "MNZ")                    ~ "MNZ",
    code %in% c("SQZ", "SQR", "SQC", "SQA", "OMZ")      ~ "SQZ",
    str_detect(code, "^RJ") | code %in% c("SKA", "RAJ") ~ "SKA",
    TRUE                                                ~ code
  )
}

harmonised_names <- c(
  JAX = "Horse mackerels",
  CTL = "Cuttlefish",
  MNZ = "Monkfish",
  SQZ = "Squids",
  SKA = "Skates and rays"
)

# Species group lookup — used in multiple landings plots
assign_species_group <- function(species_code, species_name) {
  sn <- tolower(species_name)
  case_when(
    # ---- Pelagic fish -------------------------------------------------------
    str_detect(sn, "herring|sardine|pilchard") |
      species_code %in% c("HER","PIL","SPR","SAR","SIH") |
      str_detect(sn, "^mackerel") |
      species_code %in% c("MAC","MAS") |
      str_detect(sn, "horse mackerel|scad") |
      species_code %in% c("HOM","HMM","JAA","JAX")
      ~ "Pelagic fish",

    # ---- Seaweeds -----------------------------------------------------------
    str_detect(sn, "seaweed|kelp|tangle|laminaria|fucus|ulva|algae|alga|macroalg") |
      species_code %in% c("LQD","LAH","SWX","SWA","SWB","SWC","SWD","SWE",
                           "SWF","SWG","SWH","SWI","SWJ","SWK","SWL","SWM",
                           "SWN","SWO","SWP","SWQ","SWR","SWS","SWT","SWU",
                           "SWV","SWT","SWW","ASP","ULV","FUC","LAM","ALG")
      ~ "Seaweeds",

    # ---- Cephalopods --------------------------------------------------------
    str_detect(sn, "cuttlefish|sepia") |
      species_code %in% c("CTC","CTL","CTZ","CTB","CTS","SEB","OCC")
      ~ "Cuttlefish",
    
    str_detect(sn, "squid|loligo|bobtail|ommastrep|shortfin") |
      species_code %in% c("SQC","SQR","SQE","SQM","LOL","LOG","SQS","SQZ",
                           "SQX","EUR","BOC","SQI","OMS","TOD","NBS","OMP","ILL")
      ~ "Squid",

    # ---- Demersal fish ------------------------------------------------------
    str_detect(sn, "mullet") |
      species_code %in% c("MUL","MUG","TFM","MUT","MUX")
      ~ "Mullets",
    
    str_detect(sn, "gurnard|searobin") |
      species_code %in% c("GUG","GUR","GUU","GUX","TUB","BIR")
      ~ "Gurnards",
    
    str_detect(sn, "whiting|haddock|cod") |
      species_code %in% c("WHG","HAD", "COD")
      ~ "Roundfish",
    
    species_code %in% c(
      "SOL","SOM","SOO","SOZ",
      "PLE",
      "TUR","BLL",
      "DAB","FLE",
      "MEG","LDB","MES",
      "LEM","WIT","SCL","POO",
      "HAL","GHL",
      "SXS","CET",
      "FLX","FLO","BUT","RHG"
    ) |
    str_detect(sn, "plaice|\\bsole\\b|turbot|brill|\\bdab\\b|flounder|halibut|megrim|witch|limande|cardine|fletan|plie|pliee")
      ~ "Flatfishes",

    # ---- Shellfish & invertebrates ------------------------------------------
    str_detect(sn, "scallop|pecten") |
      species_code %in% c("SCE","QSC","PEC","SCA","SCB")
      ~ "Scallops",
    str_detect(sn, "shrimp|crangon|pandalus|crevette") |
      species_code %in% c("CSH","PRA","TGS","CRG","CPR","SQS","PAN","CFW")
      ~ "Shrimps",
    
    # ---- Other shellfish & crustaceans --------------------------------------
    str_detect(sn, "whelk|buccin|crab|lobster|crawfish|langoustine|nepthrops|venus|mussel|clam|cockle|oyster") |
      species_code %in% c("WHE","BUC","CRE","SCR","LBE","NEP","VEV",
                           "MYV","MYE","COC","OYF","OYG","CLX","SCX")
      ~ "Shellfish & crustaceans",

    # ---- Other demersal fish ------------------------------------------------
    str_detect(sn, "seabream|seabass|bass|bream|pouting|bib|pollack|pollock|conger|catshark|smooth.hound|ray|skate|shark|dogfish") |
      species_code %in% c("BRB","BSS","BIB","POL","COE","SYC","SDV",
                           "RJC","RJH","RJB","RJN","RJM","RJI","SKA",
                           "DGS","DGH","SCK","SDS","GKL","MZZ")
      ~ "Other demersal fish",
    TRUE ~ NA_character_
  )
}

# ---- Pelagic data anomaly flag ----------------------------------------------
# NLD VL40XX Other/mixed pelagic landings in 27.4.C in 2012 are anomalously
# high (~84,000 t vs ~10,000 t in surrounding years), consistent with a
# sub-region misattribution in the AER source data (Channel landings apparently
# reported under 27.4.C rather than 27.7.D). Requires verification with STECF/CBS.
pelagic_species_codes <- c("HER","PIL","HOM","MAC","SPR","JAX","HMM","JAA","MAS","SAR","SIH")

pelagic_anomaly_note <- paste0(
  "* 2012 NLD pelagic landings in 27.4.C excluded due to anomalously high values ",
  "Requires verification with STECF/AER."
)

remove_pelagic_anomaly <- function(df) {
  df |>
    filter(!(country_code  == "NLD"         &
             sub_reg       == "27.4.c"      &
             year          == 2012          &
             gear_category == "Other/mixed" &
             species_code  %in% pelagic_species_codes))
}

safe_numeric <- function(x, extra_sentinels = character(0)) {
  base_pat <- "NK|na|N/A|#N/A|CONFID|confidential|BEL|\\."
  full_pat  <- if (length(extra_sentinels) > 0)
    paste0("^(", base_pat, "|", paste(extra_sentinels, collapse = "|"), ")$")
  else
    paste0("^(", base_pat, ")$")
  cleaned <- str_trim(x) |>
    str_replace_all(regex(full_pat, ignore_case = TRUE), NA_character_)
  val <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(cleaned))
  val[!is.na(val) & val == -1] <- NA_real_
  val
}

normalise_division <- function(x) {
  x <- str_trim(x) |> str_to_upper()
  x <- str_remove(x, "^27\\.")
  str_replace(x, "^(\\d+)([A-Z])$", "\\1.\\2")
}

map_gear_fdi <- function(gear_code) {
  lookup <- c(
    OTB="Bottom trawl", OTT="Bottom trawl", PTB="Bottom trawl",
    OTM="Midwater trawl", PTM="Midwater trawl",
    TBB="Beam trawl",
    SSC="Scottish seine", SDN="Danish seine",
    GNS="Gillnet", GND="Gillnet",
    FPN="Pot/trap", FPO="Pot/trap",
    LLS="Longline", LLD="Longline",
    DRB="Dredge",
    MIS="Other/mixed", NK="Unknown"
  )
  dplyr::recode(str_to_upper(str_trim(gear_code)),
                !!!lookup, .default = "Other/mixed")
}

# ==============================================================================
# table_helpers
# ==============================================================================

# ---- Shared flextable style -------------------------------------------------
# Call this on any flextable to apply consistent report formatting.
# Adjust font, size and colours once here; all tables update automatically.

style_ft <- function(ft, font_size = 6, font_name = "Calibri", total_row = TRUE) {
  n_rows <- nrow(ft$body$dataset)

  # total_row = FALSE for tables without a "Total" row in the last line
  # (otherwise the last data row is printed bold on a grey background)
  if (total_row) {
    ft <- ft |>
      flextable::bold(i = n_rows, part = "body") |>
      flextable::bg(i = n_rows, part = "body", bg = "#F2F2F2")
  }

  ft |>
    flextable::font(fontname = font_name, part = "all") |>
    flextable::fontsize(size = font_size,     part = "body") |>
    flextable::fontsize(size = font_size + 1, part = "header") |>
    flextable::bold(part = "header") |>
    flextable::bold(j = 1,      part = "body") |>        # bold row label column
    flextable::bg(part = "header", bg = "#D9E1F2") |>
    flextable::hline_top(part = "header",
                         border = officer::fp_border(width = 1.5)) |>
    flextable::hline_bottom(part = "header",
                            border = officer::fp_border(width = 1)) |>
    flextable::hline_bottom(part = "body",
                            border = officer::fp_border(width = 1.5)) |>
    flextable::colformat_num(big.mark = ",", digits = 0) |>
    flextable::set_table_properties(layout = "autofit", width = 1) |>
    flextable::align(j = -1, align = "right", part = "all") |>
    flextable::align(j = 1,  align = "left",  part = "all")
}

# ---- Shared table builder ---------------------------------------------------
make_annex_table <- function(df, row_var, col_var, value_var,
                              row_label  = row_var,
                              col_levels = NULL,
                              other_label   = "Other",
                              add_other     = TRUE,
                              add_total_row = TRUE,
                              add_total_col = TRUE,
                              caption       = NULL,
                              font_size     = 8) {

  # Lump unlisted categories into "Other"
  if (add_other && !is.null(col_levels)) {
    df <- df |>
      mutate(!!col_var := if_else(
        .data[[col_var]] %in% col_levels,
        .data[[col_var]], other_label))
  }

  # Summarise and pivot wide
  wide <- df |>
    group_by(.data[[row_var]], .data[[col_var]]) |>
    summarise(val = sum(.data[[value_var]], na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
    mutate(val = round(val)) |>
    pivot_wider(names_from  = all_of(col_var),
                values_from = val,
                values_fill = 0L)

  # Order columns: specified levels first, then Other if present
  col_order <- if (!is.null(col_levels)) {
    present <- col_levels[col_levels %in% names(wide)]
    other_present <- if (add_other && other_label %in% names(wide))
      other_label else character(0)
    c(present, other_present)
  } else {
    setdiff(names(wide), row_var)
  }
  wide <- wide |> dplyr::select(all_of(c(row_var, col_order)))

  # Total column
  num_cols <- col_order   # all non-row columns at this point
  if (add_total_col) {
    wide <- wide |>
      mutate(Total = rowSums(across(all_of(num_cols)), na.rm = TRUE))
    num_cols <- c(num_cols, "Total")
  }

  # Total row — coerce row_var to character to avoid type clash in bind_rows
  if (add_total_row) {
    total_row <- wide |>
      summarise(across(all_of(num_cols), \(x) sum(x, na.rm = TRUE))) |>
      mutate(!!row_var := "Total")          # character; matches after coercion below
    wide <- wide |>
      mutate(!!row_var := as.character(.data[[row_var]])) |>  # coerce before bind
      bind_rows(total_row)
  }

  # Rename row label column
  names(wide)[1] <- row_label

  # Build flextable
  ft <- flextable::flextable(wide) |>
    style_ft(font_size = font_size)

  if (!is.null(caption)) {
    ft <- flextable::set_caption(ft, caption = caption)
  }

  ft
}
```

```{r load-aer}
# Cache: cache_aer.RData — five objects, all pre-filtered to study_divisions_aer:
#   aer_effort_raw              (wide, one row per stratum)
#   aer_effort_summary          (aggregated by year/country/gear/sub_reg/vessel_length)
#   aer_effort_capacity_metric  (adds gt_fishdays_source + gt_fishdays_harmonised)
#   aer_landings_raw            (wide, one row per stratum × species)
#   aer_landings_summary        (aggregated by year/country/gear/sub_reg/species)
#
# Cache is invalidated when:
#   (a) the raw AER Excel file is newer than the cache, OR
#   (b) the cache exists but is missing any of the five expected objects
#       (handles caches built before an object was added)

aer_raw_mtime   <- file.mtime(aer_file)
aer_cache_mtime <- if (file.exists(aer_cache)) file.mtime(aer_cache) else as.POSIXct(0)

# Check (b): peek at saved object names without loading into global environment
aer_required_objects <- c("aer_effort_raw", "aer_effort_summary",
                           "aer_effort_capacity_metric",
                           "aer_landings_raw", "aer_landings_summary")
aer_cache_complete <- if (file.exists(aer_cache)) {
  all(aer_required_objects %in% load(aer_cache, envir = new.env()))
} else {
  FALSE
}

if (aer_cache_mtime > aer_raw_mtime && aer_cache_complete) {

  msg("AER: loading from cache (", format(aer_cache_mtime, "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M"), ")")
  load(aer_cache)

} else {

  if (!aer_cache_complete)
    msg("AER: cache incomplete (missing objects) — rebuilding ...")
  else
    msg("AER: cache stale — reading raw Excel file ...")

  aer_effort_sheet <- read_excel(aer_file, sheet = "FS_effort by sub-region ") |>
    clean_names()
  msg("AER effort sheet: ", nrow(aer_effort_sheet), " rows, ",
          ncol(aer_effort_sheet), " columns")
  msg("  variable_code values: ",
          paste(sort(unique(aer_effort_sheet$variable_code)), collapse=", "))
  msg("  sub_reg values (sample): ",
          paste(head(sort(unique(aer_effort_sheet$sub_reg)), 20), collapse=", "))

  aer_effort_raw <- aer_effort_sheet |>
    filter(!is.na(variable_code), !is.na(value)) |>
    mutate(
      year          = as.integer(year),
      sub_reg       = str_to_lower(str_trim(sub_reg)),
      gear_category = map_gear_aer(fishing_tech)
    ) |>
    # Filter to study area BEFORE pivot to reduce size
    filter(sub_reg %in% study_divisions_aer) |>
    # NOTE: fs_name is intentionally excluded from the pivot keys.
    # It is a free-text fleet segment label that can differ across rows of the
    # same stratum, which would create spurious extra rows if included.
    # year + country_code + sub_reg + fishing_tech + vessel_length + gear_category
    # form the natural stratum key; values_fn = sum handles any remaining
    # duplicates within a stratum × variable_code combination.
    dplyr::select(year, country_code, sub_reg, fishing_tech,
           vessel_length, gear_category,
           variable_code, value) |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = variable_code, values_from = value,
                values_fn = sum)

  msg("AER effort after pivot (study area): ", nrow(aer_effort_raw), " rows")
  msg("  Columns: ", paste(names(aer_effort_raw), collapse=", "))
  msg("  Countries: ", paste(sort(unique(aer_effort_raw$country_code)), collapse=", "))
  msg("  Year range: ", min(aer_effort_raw$year), "–", max(aer_effort_raw$year))

  aer_landings_sheets <- bind_rows(
    read_excel(aer_file, sheet = "FS_landings FAO 2008-2012") |> clean_names(),
    read_excel(aer_file, sheet = "FS_landings FAO 2013-2017") |> clean_names(),
    read_excel(aer_file, sheet = "FS_landings FAO 2018-2023") |> clean_names()
  )
  msg("AER landings sheets combined: ", nrow(aer_landings_sheets), " rows")

  aer_landings_raw <- aer_landings_sheets |>
    filter(!is.na(variable_code), !is.na(value)) |>
    mutate(
      year          = as.integer(year),
      sub_reg       = str_to_lower(str_trim(sub_reg)),
      gear_category = map_gear_aer(fishing_tech)
    ) |>
    # Filter to study area BEFORE pivot
    filter(sub_reg %in% study_divisions_aer) |>
    dplyr::select(year, country_code, sub_reg, fishing_tech,
           vessel_length, gear_category,
           species_code, species_name,
           variable_code, value) |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = variable_code, values_from = value,
                values_fn = sum) |>
    rename(live_weight_kg = totwghtlandg,
           value_euro     = totvallandg) |>
    mutate(live_weight_t = live_weight_kg / 1000)

  msg("AER landings after pivot (study area): ", nrow(aer_landings_raw), " rows")
  msg("  Countries: ", paste(sort(unique(aer_landings_raw$country_code)), collapse=", "))

  # Basic fishing-days summary — retains vessel_length for capacity plot
  aer_effort_summary <- aer_effort_raw |>
    group_by(year, country_code, gear_category, sub_reg, vessel_length) |>
    summarise(
      across(any_of(c("totfishdays","totseadays","totkwfishdays","totgtfishdays")),
             ~ sum(.x, na.rm = TRUE)),
      .groups = "drop"
    )

  # Capacity-weighted effort: GT-fishing days where available; impute from
  # kW-fishing days for countries that only report kW (using fleet-average ratio).
  # A flag column records the source so plots can distinguish imputed values.
  aer_effort_capacity_metric <- aer_effort_summary |>
    mutate(
      gt_fishdays_source = case_when(
        totgtfishdays > 0             ~ "GT (reported)",
        totkwfishdays > 0             ~ "GT (imputed from kW)",
        TRUE                          ~ "Not available"
      ),
      gt_fishdays_harmonised = case_when(
        totgtfishdays > 0             ~ totgtfishdays,
        totkwfishdays > 0             ~ totkwfishdays * kw_to_gt_ratio,
        TRUE                          ~ NA_real_
      )
    )

  aer_landings_summary <- aer_landings_raw |>
    group_by(year, country_code, gear_category,
             sub_reg, species_code, species_name) |>
    summarise(
      live_weight_t = sum(live_weight_t, na.rm = TRUE),
      value_euro    = sum(value_euro,    na.rm = TRUE),
      .groups = "drop"
    )

  # Both raw objects are already filtered to study_divisions_aer above,
  # so the cache contains only study-area rows — no further filtering needed.
  save(aer_effort_raw, aer_effort_summary, aer_effort_capacity_metric,
       aer_landings_raw, aer_landings_summary,
       file = aer_cache)
  msg("AER: cache saved → ", aer_cache)

  
  
  # aer_landings_sheets <- bind_rows(
  #   read_excel(aer_file, sheet = "FS_landings FAO 2008-2012") |> clean_names(),
  #   read_excel(aer_file, sheet = "FS_landings FAO 2013-2017") |> clean_names(),
  #   read_excel(aer_file, sheet = "FS_landings FAO 2018-2023") |> clean_names()
  # )  
  
  # aer_landings_sheets %>% 
  #   filter(species_code == "HER") %>% 
  #   filter(country_code == "NLD") %>% 
  #   filter(variable_code == "totwghtlandg") %>% 
  #   filter(sub_reg %in% c("27.4.a","27.4.b", "27.4.c","27.7.d")) %>% 
  #   group_by(species_name, year, sub_reg) %>% 
  #   summarise(total_t = sum(value)/1000) %>% 
  #   ggplot(aes(x=year, y=total_t, fill=sub_reg)) +
  #   geom_col(position="stack", width=0.8, na.rm=TRUE) 
    
  # rm(aer_landings_sheets)
  
}
```

```{r load-uk}
# ---- UK landings (MMO), 2020–2024 ------------------------------------------
# Raw source: uk_file (one sheet per year)
# Cache:      cache_uk.RData — uk_landings_raw, uk_landings_summary
# Delete the cache after changing map_length_uk(), map_gear_uk() or the
# nationality selection, because the cache only checks the Excel file date.

uk_cache_valid <- file.exists(uk_cache) &&
  file.mtime(uk_cache) > file.mtime(uk_file)

if (uk_cache_valid) {

  msg("UK: loading from cache (", format(file.mtime(uk_cache), "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M"), ")")
  load(uk_cache)

} else {

  msg("UK: cache missing or stale — reading raw Excel file ...")

  keep_nat <- c("UK - England", "UK - Scotland", "UK - Wales",
                "UK - Northern Ireland",
                if (include_channel_islands) c("Jersey", "Guernsey"))
  
  all_sheets <- readxl::excel_sheets(uk_file)
  msg("UK: sheets in workbook: ", paste(all_sheets, collapse = " | "))
  
  # Keep only sheets whose name contains one of the study years
  year_sheets <- all_sheets[str_detect(all_sheets, paste(uk_years, collapse = "|"))]
  msg("UK: sheets to read: ", paste(year_sheets, collapse = " | "))
  
  uk_list <- vector("list", length(year_sheets))
  
  for (i in seq_along(year_sheets)) {
    s <- year_sheets[i]
  
    # Find the header row: the first row (of the top 20) that contains "nationality"
    top <- readxl::read_excel(uk_file, sheet = s, col_names = FALSE,
                              n_max = 20, .name_repair = "minimal")
    header_row <- which(apply(top, 1, \(r) any(str_detect(
      str_to_lower(as.character(r)), "nationality"), na.rm = TRUE)))[1]
  
    if (is.na(header_row)) {
      msg("UK: sheet '", s, "' has no header row containing 'nationality'; skipped")
      next
    }
  
    df <- readxl::read_excel(uk_file, sheet = s, skip = header_row - 1) |>
      clean_names()
  
    msg("UK: sheet '", s, "': header on row ", header_row,
        ", ", nrow(df), " rows, columns: ", paste(names(df), collapse = ", "))
  
    if (!all(c("vessel_nationality", "fao_division") %in% names(df))) {
      msg("UK: sheet '", s, "' lacks vessel_nationality or fao_division; skipped")
      next
    }
  
    uk_list[[i]] <- df |>
      filter(vessel_nationality %in% keep_nat,
             str_to_lower(str_trim(fao_division)) %in% study_divisions_aer)
  }
  
  uk_landings_raw <- dplyr::bind_rows(uk_list) |>
    mutate(
      year          = as.integer(year),
      month         = as.integer(month),
      sub_reg       = str_to_lower(str_trim(fao_division)),
      country_code  = if_else(vessel_nationality %in% c("Jersey", "Guernsey"),
                              "CHI", "GBR"),
      uk_nation     = str_remove(vessel_nationality, "^UK - "),
      vessel_length = map_length_uk(length_group),
      gear_uk       = gear_category,
      gear_category = map_gear_uk(gear_category),
      live_weight_t = live_weight_tonnes,
      value_gbp     = value,
      value_euro    = value / gbp_per_eur[as.character(year)],
      source        = "UK (MMO)"
    ) |>
    filter(year %in% uk_years) |>
    dplyr::select(year, month, country_code, uk_nation, sub_reg, rectangle,
                  port_of_landing, port_nationality, vessel_length,
                  gear_uk, gear_category, species_code, species_name,
                  live_weight_t, value_gbp, value_euro, source)

  # Same structure as aer_landings_summary
  uk_landings_summary <- uk_landings_raw |>
    group_by(year, country_code, gear_category, sub_reg,
             species_code, species_name) |>
    summarise(live_weight_t = sum(live_weight_t, na.rm = TRUE),
              value_euro    = sum(value_euro,    na.rm = TRUE),
              .groups = "drop")
  # Quick sanity check, printed to the console when knitting
  uk_landings_summary |>
    group_by(year, country_code) |>
    summarise(t = round(sum(live_weight_t)), .groups = "drop") |>
    print()

  save(uk_landings_raw, uk_landings_summary, file = uk_cache)
  msg("UK: cache saved → ", uk_cache)
}
```

```{r combine-landings}
# Species codes are harmonised here (not in the caches), so changing
# harmonise_species() takes effect without rebuilding any cache.

landings_combined <- bind_rows(
  aer_landings_summary |> mutate(source = "AER (EU)"),
  uk_landings_summary  |> mutate(source = "UK (MMO)")
) |>
  mutate(
    species_code_harm = harmonise_species(species_code),
    species_name_harm = coalesce(harmonised_names[species_code_harm], species_name)
  )

# Years covered by both sources, for like-for-like totals

  filter(year %in% combined_years)
```

```{r load-gfw}

gfw_cache_mtime <- if (file.exists(gfw_cache)) file.mtime(gfw_cache) else as.POSIXct(0)

# Only stat the source files if the cache doesn't exist — avoids slow
# network/OneDrive lookups on every knit when the cache is warm.
gfw_cache_valid <- if (file.exists(gfw_cache)) {
  gfw_raw_mtime <- max(file.mtime(c(
    file.path(flyshootdir, "gfw_s7_effort.RData"),
    file.path(flyshootdir, "gfw_s6_zones.RData"),
    file.path(flyshootdir, "gfw_s3_vessel_meta.RData")
  )), na.rm = TRUE)
  gfw_cache_mtime > gfw_raw_mtime
} else {
  FALSE
}

if (gfw_cache_valid) {
  msg("GFW: loading from cache (", format(gfw_cache_mtime, "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M"), ")")
  load(gfw_cache)
} else {
  msg("GFW: cache missing or stale — loading pipeline RData files ...")
  fishing_days_study   <- load_object(
    file.path(flyshootdir, "gfw_s7_effort.RData"), "fishing_days_study")
  events_classified_fr <- load_object(
    file.path(flyshootdir, "gfw_s6_zones.RData"), "events_classified_fr")
  vessel_meta          <- load_object(
    file.path(flyshootdir, "gfw_s3_vessel_meta.RData"), "vessel_meta")
  world   <- ne_countries(scale = "medium", returnclass = "sf")
  fao_sf  <- load_object(file.path(spatialdir, "fao_sf.RData"), "fao_sf")
  fao_sf_division <- fao_sf |>
    filter(F_LEVEL == "DIVISION") |>
    dplyr::select(division = F_DIVISION) |>
    mutate(division = toupper(division)) |>
    filter(division %in% study_divisions_gfw) |>
    group_by(division) |>
    summarise(geometry = st_union(geometry)) |>
    st_make_valid()
  rm(fao_sf)
  save(fishing_days_study, events_classified_fr, vessel_meta,
       fao_sf_division, world,
       file = gfw_cache)
  msg("GFW: cache saved → ", gfw_cache)
}
```

```{r load-gfw-spatial}
# Cache: cache_gfw_spatial.RData
# Stores all expensive computed spatial objects so they survive across knits.
# Objects saved:
#   land_study, study_window_proj, study_owin,
#   world_proj, fao_div_proj,
#   bbox_7d_proj, window_7d_proj, window_7d_owin,
#   kde_results      (all-area KDE, all years)
#   kde_7d           (7D KDE, all years)
#   cell_effort_7d   (events per 5 km cell per year, 7D)
#   cell_effort_full (full grid with zeros, 7D)
#   concentration_7d (Gini + top10 per year, 7D)
#
# To force recomputation (e.g. after new GFW data):
#   file.remove(spatial_cache)

crs_proj    <- 32630
sigma_all   <- 20000   # KDE bandwidth for all-area map (m)
sigma_7d    <- 10000   # KDE bandwidth for 7D map (m)
kde_sample  <- 10000   # events sampled per year for KDE
cell_size   <- 5000    # grid cell size for concentration (m)

spatial_cache_mtime <- if (file.exists(spatial_cache)) file.mtime(spatial_cache) else as.POSIXct(0)
gfw_cache_mtime_now <- file.mtime(gfw_cache)   # spatial depends on gfw objects

if (spatial_cache_mtime > gfw_cache_mtime_now) {

  msg("GFW spatial: loading from cache (", format(spatial_cache_mtime, "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M"), ")")
  load(spatial_cache)

} else {

  msg("GFW spatial: computing spatial objects (this takes a few minutes) ...")

  # ---- Base spatial objects ------------------------------------------------
  land_study <- world %>%
    st_crop(st_bbox(c(xmin = xlim[1], xmax = xlim[2],
                      ymin = ylim[1], ymax = ylim[2]), crs = 4326)) %>%
    st_union()

  study_window_sf <- fao_sf_division %>%
    st_union() %>%
    st_difference(land_study) %>%
    st_make_valid()

  study_window_proj <- study_window_sf %>% st_transform(crs_proj)
  study_owin        <- as.owin(study_window_proj)
  world_proj        <- world           %>% st_transform(crs_proj)
  fao_div_proj      <- fao_sf_division %>% st_transform(crs_proj)

  # ---- 7D spatial objects --------------------------------------------------
  bbox_7d <- st_bbox(fao_sf_division %>% filter(division == "27.7.D"))
  land_7d <- world %>% st_crop(bbox_7d) %>% st_union()
  window_7d_sf <- fao_sf_division %>%
    filter(division == "27.7.D") %>%
    st_difference(land_7d) %>%
    st_make_valid()
  window_7d_proj <- window_7d_sf %>% st_transform(crs_proj)
  window_7d_owin <- as.owin(window_7d_proj)
  bbox_7d_proj   <- st_bbox(window_7d_proj)

  # ---- KDE — all divisions -------------------------------------------------
  events_for_kde_proj <- events_classified_fr %>%
    mutate(year = lubridate::year(start)) %>%
    filter(year %in% study_years, !is.na(lon), !is.na(lat)) %>%
    dplyr::select(year, lon, lat) %>%
    group_by(year) %>%
    slice_sample(n = kde_sample) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    st_as_sf(coords = c("lon","lat"), crs = 4326) %>%
    st_transform(crs_proj) %>%
    mutate(x = st_coordinates(.)[,1], y = st_coordinates(.)[,2]) %>%
    st_drop_geometry()

  kde_results <- map_dfr(study_years, function(yr) {
    pts <- events_for_kde_proj %>% filter(year == yr)
    if (nrow(pts) < 50) return(NULL)
    ppp_yr <- tryCatch(
      ppp(x = pts$x, y = pts$y, window = study_owin),
      error = function(e) NULL)
    if (is.null(ppp_yr)) return(NULL)
    kde <- density(ppp_yr, sigma = sigma_all, dimyx = c(200,200), edge = TRUE)
    as.data.frame(kde) %>%
      rename(x=x, y=y, density=value) %>%
      filter(!is.na(density), density > 0) %>%
      mutate(ndensity = density / max(density), year = yr)
  })

  # ---- KDE — ICES 27.7.D --------------------------------------------------
  events_7d_proj <- events_classified_fr %>%
    mutate(year = lubridate::year(start)) %>%
    filter(year %in% study_years, division == "27.7.D",
           !is.na(lon), !is.na(lat)) %>%
    dplyr::select(year, lon, lat) %>%
    st_as_sf(coords = c("lon","lat"), crs = 4326) %>%
    st_transform(crs_proj) %>%
    mutate(x = st_coordinates(.)[,1], y = st_coordinates(.)[,2]) %>%
    st_drop_geometry()

  kde_7d <- map_dfr(study_years, function(yr) {
    pts <- events_7d_proj %>% filter(year == yr)
    if (nrow(pts) < 50) return(NULL)
    ppp_yr <- tryCatch(
      ppp(x = pts$x, y = pts$y, window = window_7d_owin),
      error = function(e) NULL)
    if (is.null(ppp_yr)) return(NULL)
    kde <- density(ppp_yr, sigma = sigma_7d, dimyx = c(200,200), edge = TRUE)
    as.data.frame(kde) %>%
      rename(x=x, y=y, density=value) %>%
      filter(!is.na(density), density > 0) %>%
      mutate(ndensity = density / max(density), year = yr)
  })

  # ---- Grid-cell effort — ICES 27.7.D ------------------------------------
  events_7d_grid <- events_7d_proj %>%
    mutate(
      x_cell  = floor(x / cell_size) * cell_size + cell_size / 2,
      y_cell  = floor(y / cell_size) * cell_size + cell_size / 2,
      cell_id = paste(x_cell, y_cell, sep = "_"))

  cell_effort_7d <- events_7d_grid %>%
    group_by(year, cell_id, x_cell, y_cell) %>%
    summarise(n_events = n(), .groups = "drop")

  # Full grid (including zero-effort cells) for hotspot maps
  x_range <- seq(floor(min(cell_effort_7d$x_cell)/cell_size)*cell_size,
                 ceiling(max(cell_effort_7d$x_cell)/cell_size)*cell_size, by=cell_size)
  y_range <- seq(floor(min(cell_effort_7d$y_cell)/cell_size)*cell_size,
                 ceiling(max(cell_effort_7d$y_cell)/cell_size)*cell_size, by=cell_size)

  full_grid_sf <- expand_grid(year=study_years, x_cell=x_range, y_cell=y_range) %>%
    st_as_sf(coords=c("x_cell","y_cell"), crs=crs_proj, remove=FALSE) %>%
    st_filter(window_7d_proj %>% st_buffer(cell_size/2)) %>%
    st_drop_geometry()

  cell_effort_full <- full_grid_sf %>%
    left_join(cell_effort_7d %>% dplyr::select(year,x_cell,y_cell,n_events),
              by=c("year","x_cell","y_cell")) %>%
    replace_na(list(n_events=0)) %>%
    group_by(year) %>%
    mutate(ndensity = n_events / max(n_events)) %>%
    ungroup()

  # ---- Concentration metrics -----------------------------------------------
  concentration_7d <- cell_effort_7d %>%
    group_by(year) %>%
    summarise(
      n_cells      = n(),
      total_events = sum(n_events),
      gini         = ineq::Gini(n_events),
      top10_pct    = {
        s     <- sort(n_events, decreasing=TRUE)
        n_top <- max(1L, ceiling(0.10*length(s)))
        sum(s[seq_len(n_top)]) / sum(s) * 100
      },
      .groups = "drop")

  save(land_study, study_window_proj, study_owin,
       world_proj, fao_div_proj,
       bbox_7d_proj, window_7d_proj, window_7d_owin,
       kde_results, kde_7d,
       cell_effort_7d, cell_effort_full, concentration_7d,
       file = spatial_cache)
  msg("GFW spatial: cache saved → ", spatial_cache)
}
```

```{r load-aer-split}
# Cache: cache_aer_split.RData — single object: aer_split
#
# aer_split is the AER Bottom trawl/seine effort disaggregated to gear-code
# level using FDI proportional split keys. It contains one row per
# (year, country_code, vessel_length, sub_reg, gear_code) with columns:
#   gear_code         — OTB, OTT, PTB, SSC, SDN, or "Unsplit"
#   gear_share        — proportion of stratum days assigned to this gear_code
#   totfishdays_split — totfishdays * gear_share (conserved per stratum)
#   split_source      — "FDI direct" | "FDI pooled fallback" | "Unsplit"
#   gear_type         — "Bottom trawl (OTB/OTT/PTB)" | "Seine (SSC/SDN)" | "Unsplit"
#
# Source data: FDI gear-code CSV written by FDI_channel_analysis.R to:
#   fdi_dir/output/fdi_fishingdays_by_country_sizeclass_gearcode_division_year.csv
#
# Cache invalidated when cache_aer.RData is newer or objects are missing.
# To force rebuild: file.remove(aer_split_cache)

fdi_gearcode_csv <- file.path(fdi_dir, "output",
  "fdi_fishingdays_by_country_sizeclass_gearcode_division_year.csv")

aer_split_cache_mtime <- if (file.exists(aer_split_cache))
  file.mtime(aer_split_cache) else as.POSIXct(0)

aer_split_ok <- file.exists(aer_split_cache) &&
  aer_split_cache_mtime > file.mtime(aer_cache) &&
  "aer_split" %in% load(aer_split_cache, envir = new.env())

if (aer_split_ok) {

  msg("AER split: loading from cache (", format(aer_split_cache_mtime, "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M"), ")")
  load(aer_split_cache)

} else {

  msg("AER split: building gear-code disaggregation ...")

  if (!file.exists(fdi_gearcode_csv)) {
    msg("AER split: FDI gear-code CSV not found at:\n  ", fdi_gearcode_csv)
    msg("  Run FDI_channel_analysis.R first to generate it.")
    msg("  aer_split will not be available — Section 4.1.5 figures will be empty.")
    aer_split <- NULL
  } else {

    # ---- 1. FDI gear-code proportions per stratum ---------------------------
    # Country name to ISO3 map (FDI uses full names, AER uses ISO3)
    cty <- c(BELGIUM="BEL", DENMARK="DNK", FRANCE="FRA", GERMANY="DEU",
             IRELAND="IRL", NETHERLANDS="NLD", SWEDEN="SWE",
             "UNITED KINGDOM"="GBR", "EUROPEAN UNION"=NA_character_)

    # Gear codes that belong to the AER "Bottom trawl/seine" category
    bts_gears <- c("Bottom trawl", "Scottish seine", "Danish seine")

    # Primary split key: FDI shares per (year, country, vessel_lc, division, gear_code)
    # Shares are rescaled to sum to 1 within each stratum (handles suppressed rows).
    fdi_key <- read.csv(fdi_gearcode_csv) |>
      filter(division      %in% study_divisions_fdi,
             gear_category %in% bts_gears,
             fishing_days_sum > 0) |>
      mutate(country_code = cty[country]) |>
      filter(!is.na(country_code),
             year >= aer_years_start, year <= aer_years_end) |>          # FDI reliable 2013–2023
      group_by(year, country_code, vessel_lc, division) |>
      mutate(gear_share = fishing_days_sum / sum(fishing_days_sum)) |>
      ungroup() |>
      dplyr::select(year, country_code, vessel_lc, division, gear_code, gear_share)

    # Pooled fallback key: across all countries and years, by vessel_lc only
    # Applied where the primary key has no match (sparse countries, year gaps)
    fallback_key <- fdi_key |>
      group_by(vessel_lc, gear_code) |>
      summarise(days = sum(gear_share), .groups = "drop") |>  # sum shares as proxy weight
      group_by(vessel_lc) |>
      mutate(gear_share = days / sum(days)) |>
      ungroup() |>
      dplyr::select(vessel_lc, gear_code, gear_share)

    # ---- 2. AER base: Bottom trawl/seine, study area, 2013+ -----------------
    aer_bts <- aer_effort_summary |>
      filter(gear_category == "Bottom trawl/seine",
             sub_reg       %in% study_divisions_aer,
             year          >= aer_years_start,
             country_code  %in% report_countries_aer) |>
      mutate(division = normalise_division(sub_reg))

    # ---- 3. Primary join ----------------------------------------------------
    aer_joined <- aer_bts |>
      left_join(fdi_key,
                by = c("year", "country_code",
                        "vessel_length" = "vessel_lc", "division"))

    # ---- 4. Apply fallback for unmatched strata (one expand per missing row) -
    aer_good    <- aer_joined |> filter(!is.na(gear_share))
    aer_missing <- aer_joined |>
      filter(is.na(gear_share)) |>
      dplyr::select(-gear_code, -gear_share) |>
      left_join(fallback_key,
                by = c("vessel_length" = "vessel_lc"),
                relationship = "many-to-many") |>
      mutate(gear_share = replace_na(gear_share, 1),
             gear_code  = replace_na(gear_code,  "Unsplit"))

    # ---- 5. Combine, compute split days, label ------------------------------
    aer_split <- bind_rows(
        aer_good |> mutate(split_source = "FDI direct"),
        aer_missing |> mutate(
          split_source = if_else(gear_code == "Unsplit",
                                 "Unsplit", "FDI pooled fallback"))
      ) |>
      mutate(
        totfishdays_split = totfishdays * gear_share,
        gear_type = case_when(
          gear_code %in% c("SSC","SDN")        ~ "Seine (SSC/SDN)",
          gear_code %in% c("OTB","OTT","PTB")  ~ "Bottom trawl (OTB/OTT/PTB)",
          TRUE                                  ~ "Unsplit"
        )
      )

    # ---- 6. Conservation check ----------------------------------------------
    orig  <- aer_bts |>
      distinct(year, country_code, vessel_length, sub_reg, totfishdays) |>
      pull(totfishdays) |> sum(na.rm=TRUE)
    split <- sum(aer_split$totfishdays_split, na.rm=TRUE)
    ratio <- round(split / orig, 4)
    msg("AER split conservation: original=", round(orig),
        "  split=", round(split), "  ratio=", ratio)
    if (abs(ratio - 1) > 0.001)
      warning("Conservation check FAILED (ratio=", ratio, ")")

    save(aer_split, file = aer_split_cache)
    msg("AER split: cache saved → ", aer_split_cache)
  }
}
```

```{r uk-share, include=FALSE}
# ---- UK share of landings (used in summary, results and conclusions) -------
uk_share <- landings_combined_overlap |>
  mutate(fleet = if_else(source == "UK (MMO)", "UK", "EU")) |>
  group_by(fleet) |>
  summarise(t = sum(live_weight_t, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(pct = 100 * t / sum(t))

uk_share_pct <- round(uk_share$pct[uk_share$fleet == "UK"])

uk_share_division <- landings_combined_overlap |>
  mutate(fleet = if_else(source == "UK (MMO)", "UK", "EU")) |>
  group_by(fleet, sub_reg) |>
  summarise(t = sum(live_weight_t, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  group_by(sub_reg) |>
  mutate(pct = round(100 * t / sum(t))) |>
  ungroup()

uk_pct_div <- function(div) {
  uk_share_division$pct[uk_share_division$fleet == "UK" &
                        uk_share_division$sub_reg == div]
}
```

::: {custom-style="Hheading 1"}
Executive summary
:::

**Background and aim.** The English Channel and southern North Sea (ICES divisions 27.4.c, 27.7.d and 27.7.e) support some of the most intensively exploited fishing grounds in Europe, with important fisheries for France, the United Kingdom, Belgium and the Netherlands. Over the past decade these fisheries have been shaped by three concurrent forces: declining fish stocks, post-Brexit access restructuring, and the rapid expansion of offshore wind farms in the southern North Sea. Against this background, this report was commissioned by Cornelis Vrolijk to provide an objective, evidence-based characterisation of fishing effort, landings and spatial distribution in the study area over the period `r aer_years_start`–`r aer_years_end` (AER), `r aer_split_years_start`–`r aer_years_end` (FDI) and `r gfw_years_start`–`r max(study_years)` (GFW), with particular focus on the flyshoot segment in which the company operates. AER and FDI data were only used up to `r aer_years_end`, because the French `r aer_years_end + 1` data was not available in the AER 2025 report.

**Approach.** Four complementary data sources were integrated: the STECF Annual Economic Report (AER, STECF 25-07), providing official fishing effort and landings by EU fleet segment; UK landings data from the Marine Management Organisation (MMO), covering UK and Channel Islands vessels, which are absent from the AER after Brexit; the STECF Fisheries Dependent Information database (FDI, STECF 25-10), used to disaggregate the AER bottom trawl/seine category into conventional otter trawl (OTB) and seine (SSC/SDN) gears; and Global Fishing Watch (GFW) AIS-derived fishing event data, used for spatial analysis of effort distribution and concentration.

**Key findings.** Total (EU) fishing effort (in fishing days) in the study area declined by over 30% between `r aer_years_start` and `r aer_years_end`, driven primarily by contraction of French otter trawl and Belgian and Dutch beam trawl fleets. France dominates the effort picture throughout, contributing around 80% of AER fishing days. The Dutch flyshoot fleet, while small in absolute terms, is the dominant seine fleet in the area and has remained relatively stable. Approximately 70% of Dutch bottom trawl/seine days are attributable to flyshoot gears. EU landings are dominated by pelagic species, flatfishes, scallops, shrimps and seaweeds. Flatfish landings have declined markedly, consistent with poor stock status for Channel sole and plaice, while scallop landings have increased strongly since 2016. The AER gear category "mixed/other" encompasses both pelagic trawlers from the Netherlands and France, and French fisheries for scallops and seaweeds, making it difficult to interpret the effort trends for those fleet components.

The FDI-based gear split confirms that approximately 85–90% of bottom trawl/seine days are conventional otter trawl (predominantly French OTB), with seine gears (predominantly Dutch SSC/SDN) accounting for the remainder.

**Including the UK fleet.** Over `r min(combined_years)`–`r max(combined_years)`, UK and Channel Islands vessels accounted for around `r uk_share_pct`% of total landings in the study area, with the largest shares in 27.7.d and 27.7.e. UK landings are dominated by shellfish (whelk, scallops, cockles and crab), taken mainly by pots and traps and dredges, together with horse mackerel, flatfish and cuttlefish. EU-only (AER) figures therefore underestimate total landings in the study area by roughly 20%, and underrepresent shellfish and passive gears in particular. No UK effort data were available, so the effort trends in this report cover EU fleets only.

GFW spatial analysis reveals persistent fishing hotspots in the Pas de Calais and Baie de Seine. Dutch effort in 27.4.C shows progressive spatial compression, possibly linked to wind farm expansion. Post-Brexit restructuring is visible from 2021, with declining UK effort in 27.7.e and increased spatial separation between national fleets. Spatial concentration in 27.7.D increased from a Gini coefficient of 0.53–0.57 in 2013–2016 to 0.60–0.66 by 2019–2025, consistent with effort being compressed into a narrower spatial footprint following post-Brexit access restrictions.

**Conclusions.** The Channel and southern North Sea fisheries are undergoing long-term structural contraction in effort, accompanied by declining landings of key flatfish species and increased spatial concentration of the remaining fishing effort. The Dutch flyshoot fleet occupies a small but stable position within this system. A complete characterisation of the fisheries cannot be achieved from EU data sources alone. Complete integration of UK MMO catch and effort statistics in a future update would substantially strengthen the baseline. Quantifying the area swept per vessel-day using gear-specific swept-area coefficients is recommended as a priority next step for translating the effort trends into ecologically meaningful impact metrics.

\newpage

::: {custom-style="Hheading 1"}
Nederlandse samenvatting
:::

**Achtergrond en doel.** Het Engelse Kanaal en de zuidelijke Noordzee (ICES-vakken 27.4.c, 27.7.d en 27.7.e) behoren tot de meest intensief beviste wateren van Europa, met belangrijke visserijen voor Frankrijk, het Verenigd Koninkrijk, België en Nederland. De afgelopen jaren zijn deze visserijen beïnvloed door drie gelijktijdige ontwikkelingen: dalende visbestanden, herstructurering van de toegang na Brexit en de snelle uitbreiding van offshore windparken in de zuidelijke Noordzee. In dit kader werd dit rapport opgesteld in opdracht van Cornelis Vrolijk, met als doel een objectieve, op feiten gebaseerde beschrijving te geven van de visserij-inspanning, aanvoer en ruimtelijke verdeling in het studiegebied over de periode `r aer_years_start`–`r aer_years_end` (AER), `r aer_split_years_start`–`r aer_years_end` (FDI) en `r gfw_years_start`–`r max(study_years)` (GFW), met bijzondere aandacht voor het flyshoot-segment. AER- en FDI-gegevens werden alleen gebruikt tot en met `r aer_years_end`, omdat de Franse gegevens voor `r aer_years_end + 1` niet beschikbaar waren in het AER-rapport van 2025.

**Aanpak.** Vier complementaire databronnen zijn gecombineerd: het STECF Jaarlijks Economisch Rapport (AER, STECF 25-07) voor officiële visserij-inspanning en aanvoer per EU-vlootsegment; aanvoergegevens van de Britse Marine Management Organisation (MMO) voor Britse vaartuigen en vaartuigen van de Kanaaleilanden, die na Brexit ontbreken in de AER; de STECF Fisheries Dependent Information-database (FDI, STECF 25-10) om de AER-categorie "bordenvisserij/zegen" te splitsen in conventionele bordenvisserij (OTB) en flyshoot (SSC/SDN); en Global Fishing Watch (GFW) AIS-gebaseerde visserijdata voor ruimtelijke analyse.

**Belangrijkste bevindingen.** De totale (EU-)visserij-inspanning (in visdagen) in het studiegebied daalde met meer dan 30% tussen `r aer_years_start` en `r aer_years_end`, voornamelijk door inkrimping van de Franse bordenvisserij en de Belgische en Nederlandse boomkorvisserij. Frankrijk domineert het gehele inspanningspatroon met ongeveer 80% van de AER-visdagen. De Nederlandse flyshoot-vloot is in absolute termen klein, maar is de dominante flyshoot visserij in het gebied en bleef relatief stabiel. Ongeveer 70% van de Nederlandse *bottom trawl/seine* visdagen is toe te schrijven aan flyshoot visserij. De EU-aanvoer wordt gedomineerd door pelagische soorten, platvis, sint-jakobsschelpen, garnalen en zeewieren. De platvisaanvoer daalde sterk, consistent met de slechte bestandsstatus van tong en schol in het Kanaal, terwijl de aanvoer van sint-jakobsschelpen sterk toenam sinds 2016. De AER-vistuig categorie "overig/gemengd" omvat zowel pelagische trawlers van Nederlandse en Franse oorsprong als Franse visserijen op sint-jakobsschelpen en zeewieren, waardoor het moeilijk is de inspanningstrends voor die vlootcomponenten te interpreteren.

De FDI-gebaseerde uitsplitsing van de *bottom trawl/seine* categorie bevestigt dat ongeveer 85–90% bestaat uit conventionele bordenvisserij (overwegend Franse OTB), terwijl de flyshoot visserij (overwegend Nederlandse SSC) het resterende deel omvat.

**Britse vloot.** In `r min(combined_years)`–`r max(combined_years)` was de Britse vloot (inclusief de Kanaaleilanden) goed voor circa `r uk_share_pct`% van de totale aanvoer in het studiegebied, met de grootste aandelen in 27.7.d en 27.7.e. De Britse aanvoer bestaat vooral uit schelpdieren en schaaldieren (wulken, sint-jakobsschelpen, kokkels en krab), gevangen met potten en fuiken en dreggen, aangevuld met horsmakreel, platvis en zeekat. Cijfers die alleen op de AER zijn gebaseerd onderschatten de totale aanvoer in het studiegebied daardoor met ongeveer 20%. Britse inspanningsgegevens waren niet beschikbaar; de inspanningstrends in dit rapport betreffen alleen EU-vloten.

De GFW-ruimtelijke analyse toont persistente visserij-hotspots in het Nauw van Calais en de Seine Baai. De Nederlandse inspanning in 27.4.C vertoont progressieve ruimtelijke concentratie, waarschijnlijk gerelateerd aan de uitbreiding van windparkgebieden. De gevolgen van Brexit zijn zichtbaar vanaf 2021, met afnemende Britse inspanning in 27.7.e en toenemende ruimtelijke scheiding tussen de nationale vloten. De ruimtelijke concentratie in 27.7.D nam toe van een Gini-coëfficiënt van 0,53–0,57 in 2013–2016 naar 0,60–0,66 in 2019–2025, consistent met concentratie van de inspanning na de Brexit-toegangsbeperkingen.

**Conclusies.** De visserijen in het Kanaal en de zuidelijke Noordzee ondergaan een langdurige structurele krimp in inspanning, gepaard met dalende aanvoer van belangrijke platvissoorten en toenemende ruimtelijke concentratie van de resterende vloot in een kleiner aantal visgebieden. De Nederlandse flyshoot-vloot neemt een kleine maar stabiele positie in binnen dit systeem. Een volledige karakterisering van de visserijen is echter niet mogelijk met uitsluitend EU-databronnen. Volledige integratie van UK MMO vangst en inspannings-statistieken in een toekomstige update zou de analyse aanzienlijk versterken. Het kwantificeren van de bestreken oppervlakte per visdag via vistuig-specifieke *swept area*-coëfficiënten wordt aanbevolen als prioritaire volgende stap om de inspanningstrends te vertalen naar ecologisch betekenisvolle impactmaatstaven.

\newpage

# Introduction

## Background

This study investigates the international fisheries developments in the English Channel and Southern North Sea in the past 15 years. Over this period there has been an increase in the fisheries for squid and cuttlefish in the Channel and more recently also in the Southern North Sea. This change in fishing patterns has come under increasing public and media scrutiny, including critical coverage in the Netherlands (e.g. Follow the Money). This study attempts to provide a thorough knowledge base on the Channel and Southern North Sea fisheries using data from different sources: 1) STECF Annual Economic Report (AER, STECF 25-03 & 25-07), 2) UK landings data `r min(uk_years)`–`r max(uk_years)` (MMO, 2025), 3) STECF Fisheries Dependent Information (FDI; STECF, 2025b) and 4) Global Fishing Watch data (<https://globalfishingwatch.org>). The aim is to provide an objective, evidence-based assessment of the fisheries development in terms of effort and catches of fleets operating in the Channel and southern North Sea and the available scientific literature on those fisheries.

The report was commissioned by Cornelis Vrolijk company (<https://www.cornelisvrolijk.eu>) and executed by Martin Pastoors Fish & Fisheries.

## Objectives

-   To quantify trends in fishing effort and landings in the Channel (2008/2013–present) using official STECF (AER) and MMO statistics, with spatial distribution characterised using GFW AIS data.
-   To compile a scientifically grounded overview of the fisheries in the Channel, with particular focus on sustainability, ecosystem effects and the positioning of the flyshoot fishery.

## Study area and scope

The study covers ICES divisions 27.4.c (southern North Sea), 27.7.d (eastern English Channel) and 27.7.e (western English Channel). The combination of 27.4.c, 27.7.d and 27.7.e will be called "study area" in the report.

`r fig_nums("study_area", display="cite")` shows the study area with the ICES divisions, the bordering countries, the exclusive economic zones (EEZ) and the water depth. Most of the study area is shallower than 100 m; depths increase towards the west, where the western Channel (27.7.e) opens onto the Celtic Sea.

```{r study-area-map, fig.height=6.5, fig.width=8, fig.cap=fig_nums("study_area")}
# ---- Study area map: ICES divisions, countries and water depth ---------------
# Depth: NOAA ETOPO 2022 global relief model at 1 arc-minute (~1.8 km),
# downloaded once with marmap::getNOAA.bathy() (needs an internet connection
# and the marmap package: install.packages("marmap")).
# Depth grid and ICES division outlines are stored in cache_map.RData.
# Delete that file to rebuild, e.g. after changing map_xlim / map_ylim.
#
# EEZ boundaries: Marine Regions World EEZ v12 boundary lines (Flanders Marine
# Institute, 2023). Either set eez_file to a local copy of the boundaries
# layer (e.g. "eez_boundaries_v12.shp" from https://www.marineregions.org/downloads.php),
# or leave it NULL to download the layer once with the mregions2 package
# (install.packages("mregions2")). Stored in cache_eez.RData.

map_cache      <- file.path(cache_dir, "cache_map.RData")
map_xlim       <- c(-6.5, 7.5)     # longitude range of the map
map_ylim       <- c(48.2, 53.8)    # latitude range of the map
show_windfarms <- TRUE             # draw operational/approved wind farms
eez_cache      <- file.path(cache_dir, "cache_eez.RData")
eez_file       <- NULL             # optional local EEZ boundaries file (shp/gpkg)

if (file.exists(map_cache)) {

  msg("Map: loading depth grid and ICES divisions from cache")
  load(map_cache)   # bathy_df, ices_div_map

} else {

  msg("Map: downloading depth grid from NOAA (first knit only) ...")
  bathy_df <- tryCatch({
    b <- marmap::getNOAA.bathy(lon1 = map_xlim[1] - 0.5, lon2 = map_xlim[2] + 0.5,
                               lat1 = map_ylim[1] - 0.5, lat2 = map_ylim[2] + 0.5,
                               resolution = 1)
    marmap::fortify.bathy(b)                 # columns x (lon), y (lat), z (m)
  }, error = function(e) {
    msg("Map: depth download failed (", conditionMessage(e),
        "); the map is drawn without depth and the download is retried next knit.")
    NULL
  })

  # All ICES divisions in the map window (study divisions are highlighted below)
  s2_old <- sf::sf_use_s2()
  sf::sf_use_s2(FALSE)
  map_bbox <- sf::st_as_sfc(sf::st_bbox(c(xmin = map_xlim[1] - 1, xmax = map_xlim[2] + 1,
                                          ymin = map_ylim[1] - 1, ymax = map_ylim[2] + 1),
                                        crs = 4326))
  fao_sf <- load_object(file.path(spatialdir, "fao_sf.RData"), "fao_sf")
  ices_div_map <- fao_sf |>
    filter(F_LEVEL == "DIVISION") |>
    dplyr::select(division = F_DIVISION) |>
    mutate(division = toupper(division)) |>
    sf::st_transform(4326) |>
    sf::st_make_valid() |>
    sf::st_intersection(map_bbox) |>
    group_by(division) |>
    summarise(geometry = sf::st_union(geometry), .groups = "drop")
  rm(fao_sf)
  sf::sf_use_s2(s2_old)

  if (!is.null(bathy_df)) {
    save(bathy_df, ices_div_map, file = map_cache)
    msg("Map: cache saved → ", map_cache)
  }
}

# ---- EEZ boundaries ------------------------------------------------------------
if (file.exists(eez_cache)) {

  load(eez_cache)   # eez_lines

} else {

  eez_raw <- tryCatch({
    if (!is.null(eez_file)) {
      msg("Map: reading EEZ boundaries from ", eez_file)
      sf::st_read(eez_file, quiet = TRUE)
    } else {
      msg("Map: downloading EEZ boundaries from Marine Regions (first knit only) ...")
      mregions2::mrp_get("eez_boundaries")
    }
  }, error = function(e) {
    msg("Map: EEZ boundaries not available (", conditionMessage(e),
        "); the map is drawn without EEZs and this is retried next knit.")
    NULL
  })

  eez_lines <- NULL
  if (!is.null(eez_raw)) {
    s2_old <- sf::sf_use_s2()
    sf::sf_use_s2(FALSE)
    eez_bbox <- sf::st_as_sfc(sf::st_bbox(c(xmin = map_xlim[1] - 1, xmax = map_xlim[2] + 1,
                                            ymin = map_ylim[1] - 1, ymax = map_ylim[2] + 1),
                                          crs = 4326))
    eez_lines <- eez_raw |>
      sf::st_transform(4326) |>
      sf::st_make_valid() |>
      sf::st_intersection(eez_bbox) |>
      dplyr::select(geometry)
    sf::sf_use_s2(s2_old)
    rm(eez_raw)
    save(eez_lines, file = eez_cache)
    msg("Map: EEZ cache saved → ", eez_cache)
  }
}

# EEZ names: fixed label positions (lon, lat); adjust if labels overlap
eez_labels <- tibble::tribble(
  ~label,              ~lon,   ~lat,
  "UK EEZ",            -1.6,   50.30,
  "French EEZ",        -0.9,   49.80,
  "UK EEZ",             1.9,   52.30,
  "Belgian EEZ",        2.75,  51.45,
  "Dutch EEZ",          4.0,   52.85,
  "German EEZ",         6.6,   53.70,
  "Jersey / Guernsey", -2.6,   49.60
)

# ---- Depth classes ------------------------------------------------------------
depth_breaks <- c(0, 20, 40, 60, 80, 100, 150, 200, Inf)
depth_labels <- c("0–20", "20–40", "40–60", "60–80", "80–100",
                  "100–150", "150–200", "> 200")
depth_colours <- setNames(
  colorRampPalette(c("#EAF3FA", "#9CC3E0", "#4A8BBF", "#1F4E79"))(length(depth_labels)),
  depth_labels)

depth_df <- if (!is.null(bathy_df)) {
  bathy_df |>
    filter(z < 0) |>
    mutate(depth       = -z,
           depth_class = cut(depth, breaks = depth_breaks, labels = depth_labels,
                             include.lowest = TRUE))
} else NULL

# ---- Layers in geographic coordinates (WGS84) ---------------------------------
study_div_map <- ices_div_map |>
  filter(division %in% study_divisions_gfw)
study_div_labels <- tibble::tibble(
  division = c("27.4.C", "27.7.D", "27.7.E"),
  lon      = c(2.6, 0.6, -4.3),
  lat      = c(53.3, 50.25, 49.55)
)
other_div_labels <- ices_div_map |>
  filter(!division %in% study_divisions_gfw) |>
  sf::st_point_on_surface() |>
  mutate(lon = sf::st_coordinates(geometry)[, 1],
         lat = sf::st_coordinates(geometry)[, 2]) |>
  sf::st_drop_geometry() |>
  filter(between(lon, map_xlim[1] + 0.3, map_xlim[2] - 0.3),
         between(lat, map_ylim[1] + 0.2, map_ylim[2] - 0.2))

country_labels <- tibble::tribble(
  ~label,            ~lon,  ~lat,
  "United Kingdom",  -1.6,  52.4,
  "France",           1.5,  48.6,
  "Belgium",          4.6,  50.6,
  "Netherlands",      5.7,  52.4,
  "Germany",          7.2,  53.2,
  "Channel Islands", -2.4,  49.15
)

windfarms_map <- if (show_windfarms && exists("wind_proj")) {
  wind_proj |>
    filter(STATUS %in% c("Approved", "Production")) |>
    sf::st_transform(4326)
} else NULL

# ---- Plot ---------------------------------------------------------------------
p_map <- ggplot()

if (!is.null(depth_df)) {
  p_map <- p_map +
    geom_raster(data = depth_df, aes(x = x, y = y, fill = depth_class)) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = depth_colours, name = "Depth (m)", drop = FALSE)
}

p_map <- p_map +
  geom_sf(data = ices_div_map, fill = NA, colour = "grey45",
          linewidth = 0.3, linetype = "dotted")

if (!is.null(eez_lines)) {
  p_map <- p_map +
    geom_sf(data = eez_lines, colour = "#8B1A1A", linewidth = 0.45,
            linetype = "dashed")
}

if (!is.null(windfarms_map)) {
  p_map <- p_map +
    geom_sf(data = windfarms_map, fill = "grey20", colour = "grey20",
            linewidth = 0.1, alpha = 0.6)
}

p_map <- p_map +
  geom_sf(data = world, fill = "grey88", colour = "grey55", linewidth = 0.25) +
  geom_sf(data = study_div_map, fill = NA, colour = "black", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_text(data = other_div_labels, aes(x = lon, y = lat, label = division),
            size = 2.4, colour = "grey35") +
  geom_label(data = study_div_labels, aes(x = lon, y = lat, label = division),
             size = 3.2, fontface = "bold", fill = alpha("white", 0.8),
             label.size = 0) +
  geom_text(data = country_labels, aes(x = lon, y = lat, label = label),
            size = 3, fontface = "italic", colour = "grey25") +
  { if (!is.null(eez_lines))
      geom_text(data = eez_labels, aes(x = lon, y = lat, label = label),
                size = 2.6, colour = "#8B1A1A") } +
  coord_sf(crs = 4326, xlim = map_xlim, ylim = map_ylim, expand = FALSE) +
  labs(title    = "Study area: English Channel and southern North Sea",
       subtitle = "ICES divisions 27.4.c, 27.7.d and 27.7.e (bold outline)",
       caption  = paste0("Depth: NOAA ETOPO 2022 (1 arc-minute). Dotted grey lines: other ICES divisions.",
                         if (!is.null(eez_lines))
                           " Dashed red lines: EEZ boundaries (Marine Regions, World EEZ v12).",
                         if (!is.null(windfarms_map))
                           " Dark grey: offshore wind farms (operational or approved)."),
       x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(panel.background = element_rect(fill = "#EAF3FA"),
        panel.grid       = element_line(colour = "white", linewidth = 0.2),
        legend.position  = "right",
        plot.caption     = element_text(size = 7, colour = "grey40")) +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(ncol = 1))

p_map
```

Because the French AER data for `r aer_years_end + 1` has not been reported in STECF 2025-03/2025-07, the period of analysis has been restricted to `r aer_years_start`–`r aer_years_end` for effort and landings trends. The GFW analyses have been carried out for `r gfw_years_start`–`r max(study_years)` for spatial analysis.

# Material & Methods

This report combines four data sources, each covering a different period and providing different information. `r fig_nums("data_overview", display="cite")` gives an overview: the AER provides the long-term series of EU effort and landings, the MMO data add the landings of the UK and Channel Islands fleets from `r min(uk_years)` onwards, the FDI data are used only to split the AER bottom trawl/seine category into otter trawl and seine, and the GFW data are used only for the spatial analysis. The sources are described in detail in Sections `r sec["aer"]`–`r sec["gfw"]`.


## STECF AER data (effort and landings trends)

The Annual Economic Report (AER) data were obtained from the STECF 25-07 data release (*EU Fleet Economic and Transversal data, fleet segment level*). The AER provides fishing effort (fishing days, sea days, kW-days, GT-days) and landed weight and value by fleet segment (country × fishing technique × vessel length class), disaggregated by FAO division.

The AER analyses in this report cover the period `r aer_years_start`–`r aer_years_end`. The end year of `r aer_years_end` reflects the absence of French effort and landings data for `r aer_years_end + 1` in the current STECF 25-07 release. The AER data does not distinguish between bottom trawl and seine fisheries; they are reported as a combined category.

The AER does not contain data for the United Kingdom following its departure from the EU. UK landings were therefore obtained separately from the UK Marine Management Organisation (Section `r sec["uk"]`). No comparable UK effort data were available for this report.

### Vessel length classes

The AER reports effort and landings by vessel length class (VLC), defined by overall length (LOA) in metres. Six standard classes are used throughout this report, as defined in the STECF fleet data collection framework:

```{r vlc-table, echo=FALSE}
tibble::tibble(
  `Code`              = c("VL0010","VL1012","VL1218","VL1824","VL2440","VL40XX"),
```

### Species groups

Landings in the AER are reported at the individual species level using FAO 3-alpha species codes. For summary figures and tables, individual species are aggregated into ecologically and commercially meaningful species groups. The grouping was applied using FAO 3-alpha codes as the primary key (reliable and consistent across member states) with species name pattern matching as a fallback. `r tab_nums("spp_group_table", display="cite")` lists the species groups used and the main constituent species.

## UK Landings data (MMO)

UK landings were obtained from the dataset underlying the UK Sea Fisheries Statistics 2024 (MMO, 2025), covering landings by UK vessels into all ports and landings by non-UK vessels into UK ports for `r min(uk_years)`–`r max(uk_years)`. The dataset reports monthly landings by vessel nationality, ICES division and statistical rectangle, port of landing, vessel length group, gear category and species, as live weight, landed weight and first-sale value (GBP).

**Selection.** Only vessels of UK nationality (England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland) were retained, together with vessels from Jersey and Guernsey, which are reported separately as Channel Islands (CHI). Landings by non-UK vessels into UK ports were excluded, because these are already included in the AER data of the respective flag states. The data were restricted to ICES divisions 27.4.c, 27.7.d and 27.7.e.

**Harmonisation with the AER.** UK vessel length groups were mapped onto the AER vessel length classes (`r tab_nums("vlc_table", display="cite")`) using the lower bound of each length group. UK gear categories were mapped onto the AER gear categories as shown in `r tab_nums("uk_gear_map", display="cite")`. The original UK gear categories were retained in addition; unlike the AER, they distinguish demersal trawls from demersal seines. Species are coded with FAO 3-alpha codes in both sources, but some species are reported under different codes. Horse mackerel (HOM/JAX), cuttlefish (CTC/CTL), monkfish (ANF/MON/MNZ), squids (SQC/SQR/SQZ) and skates and rays (RJx/SKA) were therefore harmonised to a common code before species grouping (Section `r sec["spp"]`). Live weight was used throughout, consistent with the AER. Values were converted from GBP to EUR using annual average ECB exchange rates.

**Limitations.** The UK data cover landings only; no UK effort data were available, so UK vessels are absent from all effort figures. The UK series starts in `r min(uk_years)`, so pre-Brexit UK landings cannot be compared with post-Brexit landings. Direct comparisons between EU and UK landings are restricted to `r min(combined_years)`–`r max(combined_years)`, the years covered by both sources. Spatial attribution may differ slightly between sources: UK landings are attributed to the reported rectangle and division, while AER landings by sub-region are compiled by Member States from logbook and sales-note data.
